A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAIL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and the appendices report original Brax and MinAtar experiments, reward-function ablations, and comparisons with adversarial and non-adversarial imitation methods.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds regularization tests, evolutionary-search repetitions, OpenES comparisons, and additional divergence-based comparisons.

M1.justification: DAIL retains the reward function in Equation 4, the meta-learning objective, and Algorithms 1–2. The prompts and evolutionary procedure are unchanged; additional discovered functions are experimental outputs.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five Brax tasks and three MinAtar games. The additional Breakout discovery experiment reuses an existing task. Atari-57, Procgen, and larger discovery suites appear only as future directions.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against OpenES, Pearson chi-squared, squared-Hellinger, total-variation, and Wasserstein-GAIL methods in Tables 10–11. The original GAIL, AIRL, FAIRL, GAIL-heuristic, BC, and IQ-Learn comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The evaluation design expands to five discriminator-regularization regimes, a matched budget of 200 inner-loop evaluations for OpenES, an additional Breakout discovery experiment, and a WGAIL learning-rate sweep selecting 0.003. Original demonstration sampling, PPO/A2C settings, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 tests sensitivity to discriminator regularization, repeatability across independent searches, discovery on another retained task, and the contribution of LLM guidance through OpenES. These substantially extend the original entropy, density-ratio, and reward-component analyses.

E5.justification: Section 6.4 explicitly adds a second independent SpaceInvaders evolutionary run. The existing 16-seed policy evaluations, SEM reporting, and four-seed 95% confidence intervals for the non-adversarial comparison are retained.

E6.justification: New results show DAIL leading GAIL overall under three of five regularization regimes and leading the additional divergence baselines on five of seven tasks. Table 10 reports DAIL/OpenES returns of 0.90/0.73 on SpaceInvaders but 0.66/1.27 on Asterix. Table 8 adds discoveries from two further searches. Original plotted results and the BC/IQ-Learn table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 instantiates the existing variational derivation for additional divergences, including squared Hellinger, Pearson chi-squared, and total variation in Table 3. Appendix I adds the Lipschitz-constrained Wasserstein discriminator objective in Equation 38. Existing lemmas and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: discovering reward-assignment functions through LLM-guided evolution, introducing DAIL as the first meta-learned AIL algorithm, and demonstrating generalization and improved training behavior.

C2.justification: v2 interprets similar repeated discoveries as search stability and suggests that OpenES reward-function irregularity contributes to weaker performance. It adds computational limits on broader benchmark testing and drops the explicit statistical-significance assertion for probability of improvement. The original mechanism explanation and static-function limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the rliable library and documents settings for added comparisons, including WGAIL’s selected learning rate. It removes the abstract’s explicit public code link while retaining the supplementary-code statement. Original prompts, hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and runtime values remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds acknowledgment of Ke et al. (2021), Zhang et al. (2020), and Teoh et al. (2025). New future-work citations cover larger benchmarks and discovery efforts. The central research positioning remains stable; removal of bibliography URLs does not remove the cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and citation edits, updates author affiliations and publication headers, and adds acknowledgments, Section 6.4, and two comparison appendices. The overall narrative and most existing explanations retain their structure.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with regularization, divergence-definition, OpenES, and additional-baseline tables, plus two new figures. The discovered-function table gains environment/run groupings and ten functions. All eight original figures are retained, with some relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked independent search repetitions and a non-LLM search control. v2 addresses these important evidential gaps and adds regularization and broader baseline comparisons, strengthening the central empirical case while revealing conditions where DAIL loses. The removed public code link and limited OpenES implementation detail weaken reproducibility, but the new controls provide a substantial net improvement.
